title: Domain data migration workshop

stages.name: recoverSourceMeaning
stages.algorithm: Reconcile dictionaries, sample records, application notes, and domain-owner explanations. Identify fields whose meaning depends on record type or history, and distinguish null, not applicable, unknown, and deliberately withheld values before proposing transformations.
stages.gate: No target mapping based solely on field names or observed value formats.

stages.name: designMappings
stages.algorithm: Construct conditional field and entity mappings that preserve domain meaning. Identify lossy transformations, required target extensions, and records needing manual resolution; do not invent missing facts to satisfy a stricter target schema.
stages.gate: Every mapping declares its domain, missing-value behavior, and information loss.

stages.name: resolveRecords
stages.algorithm: Apply mappings to bounded record groups, resolving semantic exceptions through evidence-backed decisions. Preserve identity and relationship provenance, isolate incompatible records, and avoid forcing all source variants into one target category for completion metrics.
stages.gate: Accepted target records satisfy schema and source-meaning checks.

stages.name: rehearseMigration
stages.algorithm: Materialize a staged target snapshot, validate referential integrity and business invariants, and compare representative source-target round trips. Rehearse rollback and delta capture so cutover does not lose changes made after the initial extraction.
stages.gate: Exact counts, relationships, conservation constraints, and reversible mappings verified.

stages.name: coordinateCutover
stages.algorithm: Freeze the approved mapping and cutover scope, apply final source deltas, and reconcile target results before switching consumers. Track quarantined records and post-cutover corrections explicitly, retaining a safe rollback or forward-repair plan for irreversible changes.
stages.gate: No unaccounted source record or unapproved mapping change during cutover.

operational_details: A source system reuses identifiers: include system and historical validity in identity keys.
A null has several meanings: preserve explicit missing-state categories in the target.
Source data changes during migration: capture and replay deltas against the approved mapping version.
A target constraint cannot represent a valid source case: propose a schema extension or quarantine, not fabricated data.
Rollback would overwrite new target work: use an explicit reconciliation plan.
